turns.doctor_question: How long have you been hearing these voices?
turns.patient_response:
Well, if I really sit down and trace it back... let me think. It was right around the end of the previous quarter. Yes, so that would make it about three months ago. I remember the timeline specifically because we were in the middle of preparing all the Q3 deliverables for the board, and I was working late most nights to ensure the margins looked exactly right before the presentation. 

I was sitting in my office, it must have been past 8 PM, and the executive floor was practically deserted. The cleaning staff had already done their rounds, so it was just me. And that's when I first noticed it coming through the conference room walls. At first, I just assumed one of the VPs had left a dial-in meeting running on the Polycom system, you know how people forget to disconnect the line? So I actually got up, walked down the hall, and went to check. The room was pitch black. The system was off. But I could still hear them talking about my leadership. 

And then, maybe a week after that, the issue with my phone started. So, yes, it's been a solid three months of this. Ninety days of just... relentless, unavoidable commentary. It's ironic, really, because in business, a quarter is the standard metric for evaluating performance, right? You measure everything in 90-day increments. And for this entire past quarter, for the last three months exactly, I've had to navigate this situation where they are just actively broadcasting their criticisms through the drywall and my completely powered-off smartphone. Three months of having to double-check if my screen is even lit up before I realize they're doing it again. It's just been a very long three months, Doctor.

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any diagnosed medical conditions or physical health problems?

Medical conditions? No, no, nothing like that. I've always been remarkably healthy, actually. I mean, you have to be, don't you? When you're carrying the weight of an entire corporation on your shoulders, you can't afford to be calling in sick or taking weeks off for medical leave. The board wouldn't tolerate it, and frankly, I wouldn't tolerate it from myself. 

I actually had my annual executive physical—our firm requires it for all C-suite officers, it's a whole comprehensive workup they do over at the private clinic downtown—just about six months ago. They check everything. Blood panels, EKG, stress tests, the works. The physician there, Dr. Aris, he actually joked that I have the cardiovascular profile of someone ten years younger. He said my numbers were pristine. So, no diabetes, no high blood pressure, no thyroid issues... nothing. 

I don't even get seasonal colds, to be honest. I think when you operate at this level of adrenaline and responsibility, your immune system just sort of falls in line. You simply don't have the time to be unwell. I take my daily vitamins, I stay hydrated, I try to get a decent amount of sleep when the deliverables allow for it. But no, there are no underlying physical health problems whatsoever. My body is functioning perfectly. It's just... it's just this external interference, this constant barrage of criticism coming through the walls and the electronics. If it weren't for that, I'd be operating at 100 percent capacity. So physically, medically? I'm completely fine. Perfect bill of health.
